frequency_question: What proportion of sudden bilateral commercial embargoes by a Gulf state are reversed or significantly relaxed within 365 days?
membership_rule: Includes official, government-decreed halts to trade, commercial exchange, or financial transactions directed at a specific state by a GCC member. Excludes multilateral UN sanctions or purely tariff-based disputes.

cases.name: UAE partial diplomatic and economic downgrade with Iran

coverage_note: 2 named; universe of comparable sudden unilateral Gulf commercial embargoes is very small.
known_gaps: Few exact historical parallels exist for an overnight total commercial ban by the UAE on Iran specifically, making these broader regional analogues necessary.
skeleton: 2 major regional diplomatic-commercial rupture episodes in the Gulf involving the UAE or close GCC allies over the last 15 years, where the average time to partial or full normalization/reversal was greater than 365 days for deep structural disputes but under 365 days for tactical downgrades.
multiplier: 1 out of 2 reversed within one year.
validity_reason: Regional security architecture and GCC decision-making norms evolve slowly over multi-year cycles.
